title: Before God Trusts You With the Platform, He Will Meet You in the Wilderness
paragraphs:
Before God Trusts You With the Platform, He Will Meet You in the Wilderness
The Hidden Reason Heaven Seems Silent—And Why Your Loneliest Season May Be the Greatest Evidence That God Is Preparing You, Not Abandoning You
There is a place almost nobody wants to stay.
It is the place where prayers seem unanswered.
Where silence becomes louder than every sermon you've ever heard.
The Bible calls that place the wilderness.
Most people think the wilderness is where God leaves His people.
The wilderness is where God prepares them.
If you're there today, this article is not an accident.
"God... why does everything feel so difficult when all I want is to follow You?"
"What if this difficult season is the evidence that God is preparing me for something I could never survive without Him?"
Because from Genesis to Revelation, one pattern keeps appearing.
Not because God enjoys watching His children suffer.
But because God loves them too much to release them before they are ready.
The Hebrew word most often translated "wilderness" is מִדְבָּר (midbār).

Interestingly, midbār is closely related to the Hebrew root דָּבַר (dābar), meaning "to speak" or "word." While linguistically they are distinct forms, biblical scholars have long noticed the powerful theological connection: the wilderness is repeatedly the place where God speaks to His people.
That is exactly what Scripture shows.
John the Baptist found his voice.
Even Jesus entered the wilderness before beginning His public ministry.
The wilderness often becomes the place where distractions are removed so God's voice becomes unmistakably clear.
That should completely reshape how we view hardship.
The wilderness is not God's absence.
Israel spent forty years wandering through barren land.
Yet Deuteronomy explains God's deeper purpose.

"He humbled you and let you hunger and fed you with manna... that He might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD." (Deuteronomy 8:3)
God was exposing what their hearts truly depended upon.
Sometimes God removes earthly security because He wants to become our greatest security.
Moses understood this better than anyone.
At forty years old he believed he was ready to rescue Israel.
He tried accomplishing God's purpose using human strength.
Imagine wondering whether your life had become one giant mistake.
Only after decades of obscurity did God appear in the burning bush.
And dependence became the foundation of one of history's greatest callings.
Samuel anointed him king while he was still a shepherd.
But the throne did not come immediately.
Years passed between God's promise and God's fulfillment.
Because kings are not made by crowns.
A shepherd can wear a crown.
But only a broken servant can carry one faithfully.
After standing courageously against hundreds of false prophets on Mount Carmel, he fled into the wilderness overwhelmed, exhausted, and asking God to let him die.
But through what the Hebrew text describes as קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה (qōl demāmāh daqqāh)—literally, "a sound of thin silence" or "a gentle whisper" (1 Kings 19:12).
Sometimes God speaks loud enough for crowds.
Sometimes He speaks quietly enough that only surrendered hearts can hear Him.
The greatest example, however, is Jesus Himself.
The Spirit led Him into the wilderness.
Matthew does not say Satan led Him there.
"Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil." (Matthew 4:1)
That sentence changes how we understand hardship.
The wilderness was not outside God's plan.
It was part of God's preparation.
Yet every temptation revealed perfect obedience.
The perfect tense emphasizes that God's written Word remains permanently authoritative.
Jesus defeated temptation not by inventing new truth but by standing on the truth already revealed.
That alone should transform how we fight our own battles.
Or maybe your wilderness is hidden behind smiles while your soul quietly asks,
If you belong to Christ, God's silence is never proof of His absence.
Sometimes silence is where deeper trust grows.
Faith does not become mature when every prayer is answered immediately.
Faith becomes mature when we continue walking with Jesus even when the path ahead is hidden.
"Count it all joy... when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness."
That is why wilderness seasons cannot be skipped.
A public calling without private surrender eventually collapses.
Only Christlike character can sustain the weight of influence.
Even Paul experienced this divine pattern.
After his dramatic encounter with Christ, he did not immediately become the missionary the world remembers.
There were years of hidden preparation before the great missionary journeys.
God often develops roots long before He grows branches.
Because storms reveal whether roots truly exist.
Perhaps you have been measuring God's love by your circumstances.
Scripture invites us to measure His love by the Cross instead.
The Cross forever settled the question of whether God loves us.
Everything afterward—including wilderness seasons—is interpreted through Calvary.
The Cross declares that God's heart is for His people.
The Resurrection declares that no wilderness lasts forever.
The Gospel declares that our greatest wilderness was not geographical.
Humanity wandered in sin, separated from God.
This is why our message has always been...
Because every believer has a story that begins in brokenness and finds its true ending in Christ.
Jesus does not merely improve lives.
Perhaps today your wilderness feels like failure.
Jesus is building a heart that will not be destroyed by the door He eventually opens.
The greatest tragedy is not walking through a wilderness.
The greatest tragedy is leaving it without learning to trust the One who walked there before us.
If this message found you exactly when you needed it, don't let it end with you.
God often uses an ordinary share to place extraordinary hope in front of someone who is one prayer away from giving up.
Sometimes we need to preach yesterday's truth to today's fears.
If your desire is truly to glorify God, partnering in the spread of His truth is one practical way to participate in the Great Commission.
One day you'll discover that the place you begged God to remove became the place where He made you ready.
